faqs.q: Sec. 102-411. - Appeals of a determination or order of the director.
faqs.a:
(a)
Filing; timeliness.
A property owner who is aggrieved by a notice or order of the director issued under
section 102-408
may appeal that order on a form prescribed by the city and available from the director
               on the city's website or by hard copy. The appeal must be in writing and be submitted
               to the city clerk within 14 days of the date of the director's order. An appeal form
               that is not complete in all respects or that does not state the grounds for appeal
               shall be promptly returned by the clerk to the property owner. The property owner
               may resubmit an appeal form deemed incomplete by the clerk, and the clerk shall accept
               it, if the resubmitted form is complete and submitted to the clerk within the deadline
               set forth in this subsection. Compliance with the 14-day time limit noted in this
               subsection (a) shall be a jurisdictional prerequisite to any appeal brought under
               this article. Failure to comply shall bar any such appeal.
(b)
Grounds.
The appeal shall be based on a claim that:
(1)
The provisions of this article do not apply; or
(2)
The true intent of this article has been incorrectly interpreted by the director;
               or
(3)
The property owner has previously filed with the director written documentation outlining
               the replacement of LSL or request for extension of time which has been rejected by
               the director.
(c)
Procedure.
The appeal form, and any other documentation submitted to the city clerk by the property
               owner, as well as any response or documentation submitted by the director, will be
               submitted by the city clerk to the city manager or designee thereof for review. Notwithstanding
               any other provision of this Code, the appeal of the director's order shall consist
               of a review of all relevant documentation on file with the city in the case, as well
               as the appeal form and any accompanying materials. All documents may be reviewed electronically.
               The city bears the burden of proof in an appeal to establish that the director's action
               or determination was reasonable in light of the intent of this article, that the terms
               of this article applied to the property owner in question. The city manager or designee
               thereof shall review the information submitted, and within 14 days of the date of
               the filing of the appeal, issue a written decision on the appeal. The decision must
               contain the reason or reasons for the decision. The decision must set forth appeal
               rights, if any. The decision may be mailed by first class U.S. Mail or furnished to
               the property owner electronically. Should the city manager or designee thereof fail
               to issue a written decision on the appeal within the time frame set forth herein,
               the claim shall be deemed denied, and the property owner may proceed as if an adverse
               decision has been issued.
(d)
Appeal of city manager's decision.
The city manager's decision, or denial of an appeal as a result of the manager's
               failure to issue a written decision, shall be considered a final agency decision.
               The appeal may proceed under Rule 106 of the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure.
(
Ord. No. 4869
, § 1, 3-4-2024)
